analysis: Increasing uniform negatives from 8 to 64 did not improve validation: pinned-host macro HR@10 was 0.5600 versus 0.5613 for eight negatives (−0.0013), and below the historical binary-loss GRURec result of 0.5737. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.585, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.585, Electronics 0.475, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.595. Prior category scores were not supplied, so category-level regressions cannot be established. Macro HR@20 was 0.6850 versus the reported eight-negative result of 0.6900. The trial succeeded operationally, consuming 251.80 allocated GPU-seconds, but provides no evidence that insufficient negative competition caused the earlier regression. The small HR@10 difference alone does not establish a reliable disadvantage.
code_summary: One independently trained GRURec per category: 96-dimensional item embeddings, input LayerNorm, dropout 0.25, a two-layer GRU, and linear/LayerNorm projection. Scores use normalized hidden and item representations, a learned scale capped at 30, and jointly trained item biases. The sole experimental change was increasing NEGATIVES from 8 to 64 for 65-class sampled-softmax cross-entropy. Uniform sampling, positive-collision resampling, and duplicate negatives were retained. Training uses AdamW, mixed precision on CUDA, gradient clipping, validation-selected checkpoints, and early stopping. The predictor routes each of the four categories to exactly one trained checkpoint; no ensemble or checkpoint averaging is used.
